(a) **Absolute Configurations:**
- (i) Applying Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) priority rules: $-\text{OH}$ (1), $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (2), $-\text{CH}_3$ (3), $-\text{H}$ (4). With $-\text{H}$ horizontal/vertical, assign configuration accordingly. Standard Fischer projection gives **(S)** configuration.
- (ii) Multi-chiral center assignment yields respective configuration based on standard priority rules: **(2R, 3S)**.
- (iii) Substituted biphenyl system with restricted rotation showing axial chirality: **(R)** or **(S)** based on directional priority of ortho-substituents.

(b) **Spiro Compounds:** Compounds containing two or more rings sharing a single common atom (known as the spiro atom). *Example:* Spiro[3.3]heptane.

(c) **Inductive vs Mesomeric Effect:**
| Inductive Effect ($I$-effect) | Mesomeric Effect ($M$-effect) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Permanent displacement of $\sigma$-electrons. | Permanent delocalization of $\pi$-electrons. |
| Distance-dependent (decreases rapidly along chain). | Distance-independent (operates through conjugation). |

(d) **Circular Dichroism (CD):**
- **Definition:** The differential absorption of left-handed and right-handed circularly polarized light by optically active chiral molecules.
- **Uses:** Determination of absolute configuration, protein secondary structure analysis (folding/unfolding), and study of nucleic acids.
proTip: Always prioritize groups using CIP rules correctly before assigning R/S configurations.
